title: Spotify Stock Is Down 26%. Should You Buy the Dip, or Run for the Hills?
detail:
Spotify Stock Is Down 26%. Should You Buy the Dip, or Run for the Hills?
Anthony Di Pizio, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 4:25 AM CDT 6 min read
SPOT
NVDA
MU
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

When it comes to artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, investors tend to think of chip giants like Nvidia or Micron Technology. But AI is starting to create value for many companies, even those not operating at the industry's frontier, and that spells an opportunity for investors.

Spotify (NYSE: SPOT) runs the world's largest music streaming platform, and it's betting big on AI to enhance the listening experience, which is boosting engagement and, therefore, revenue. The company reported a strong set of operating results for the third quarter of 2026 (ended Sept. 30) last week, which sent its stock soaring by more than 11%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But the stock is still down 26% from last year's record high as I write this on Oct. 27, so should investors take this opportunity to buy the dip, or will the recent recovery run out of steam?

Image source: Getty Images.
Artificial intelligence is transforming Spotify

Most music streaming services offer the same content catalog, because a small handful of record labels control most of the industry's rights, and they want their artists to reach as many listeners as possible. That means the primary way Spotify can differentiate its platform from the competition is by delivering a better user experience, and AI is central to its strategy.

AI is embedded in Spotify's recommendation algorithm, where it learns what type of music each user likes, so it can feed them more of it. AI also powers a growing number of features, like Prompted Playlist which will curate a basket of songs based on a description provided by the user. But management is aiming to turn Spotify into the world's first agentic media platform, which will introduce a range of unique capabilities, and some of them are already live.

For example, users can ask Spotify to analyze their listening history dating all the way back to 2008, and surface their favorite songs. It can also ask the platform to mix tracks together to create the perfect playlist, organized by factors like beats per minute. It can also recap an audiobook the user is listening to, up until the point they previously stopped.

Spotify can integrate with third-party agentic systems like OpenAI's Dots and Meta Platforms' Muse, enabling users to control their audio environment while completing other tasks. For example, users can ask Muse to build a playlist through Spotify, tailored to a specific road-trip destination.

For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 29, 2026 – Zacks Equity Research shares Eni E as the Bull of the Day and Burlington Stores BURL as the Bear of the Day. In addition, Zacks Equity Research provides analysis on Spotify Technology S.A. SPOT, Equifax EFX and ManpowerGroup MAN.

Here is a synopsis of all five stocks:

Bull of the Day:

Italian energy giant Eni is emerging as a compelling oil and gas stock to consider as surging crude oil prices and improving earnings expectations fuel optimism across the energy sector.

With geopolitical tensions and supply disruptions pushing crude prices higher, Eni's Zacks Oil and Gas – Integrated – International Industry currently ranks in the top 3% of more than 240 Zacks industries, highlighting strong momentum across the energy sector.

Furthermore, Eni's diversified portfolio spans oil and gas production, refining, liquefied natural gas (LNG), and renewable energy, offering investors multiple avenues for long-term growth.

Even after soaring nearly 70% year-to-date and trading near its 52-week high of $62 a share, Eni's valuation remains attractive, suggesting additional upside potential.

Eni's Earnings Estimates Are Surging

Most appealing is the sharp upward trend in Eni's earnings estimates, with analysts becoming increasingly bullish on the company's profitability.

Over the last 60 days, fiscal 2026 EPS estimates have jumped 15% from $5.77 to $6.65 per share and would equate to 90% year-over-year growth, while FY27 EPS projections have surged 25% in the last two months from $5.08 to $6.38 per share.

Near-term expectations are even more encouraging, with earnings estimates for the next two quarters rising 43% and 59%, respectively.

These substantial upward revisions reflect growing confidence in Eni's earnings outlook and suggest that its recent rally has been supported by improving fundamentals.

Eni's Attractive Valuation & Revenue Base

Despite its impressive performance, Eni stock still trades at just 9X forward earnings and less than 1X annual sales, representing an appealing valuation for a global integrated energy company.

Furthermore, Eni is expected to generate more than $100 billion in annual revenue for the foreseeable future, providing a substantial business foundation from which even modest margin improvements could translate into meaningful earnings growth.

Eni's Generous Dividend Has Plenty of Room to Grow

Adding to its appeal, Eni offers an attractive annual dividend of $1.68 per share, yielding 2.85% at current levels.

Eni has also increased its dividend at an annualized rate of 6.31% over the last five years, demonstrating its commitment to rewarding shareholders.

More importantly, Eni's modest 30% payout ratio suggests there is plenty of room for future dividend hikes, especially as improving earnings expectations strengthen the company's profitability outlook.

Bottom Line

Sporting a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), Eni stands out as an attractive energy stock as rising earnings estimates and industry strength reinforce its bullish outlook.

Although shares have rallied considerably, Eni's reasonable valuation, substantial revenue base, and improving earnings potential suggest there could still be more upside ahead.

Bear of the Day:

Off-price retail giant Burlington Stores has struggled in 2026, with shares plunging almost 40% in the last three months and now down nearly 20% year-to-date as declining earnings expectations raise concerns about the retailer's near-term profitability.

Despite the selloff, BURL shares still trade well above $200, and unfavorable earnings estimate revisions suggest investors may want to remain cautious as the stock could face additional downside.

Burlington's Declining Earnings Estimates

Burlington's near-term profitability outlook has weakened with management expecting Q3 adjusted earnings of $1.60-$1.70 per share, down from $1.80 a year ago, as operating margins face pressure from merchandise pricing investments and softer consumer spending.

Furthermore, comparable-store sales growth most recently slowed to 2% in Q2 from 5% a year earlier, raising questions about underlying demand as inflation and elevated living costs weigh on budget-conscious shoppers.

Most concerning is the negative trend in Burlington's earnings estimate revisions, with analysts becoming increasingly cautious about the company's outlook.

Over the last 60 days, Burlington's current fiscal-year EPS estimate has fallen 5.5% from $12.61 to $11.92 per share, while next year's projection has declined 4.6% from $13.87 to $13.23 per share.

Near-term expectations have also weakened, with earnings estimates for the next two quarters falling roughly 7.6% and 3.2%, respectively.

Rising Costs & Slowing Sales Threaten Burlington's Margins

Compounding these challenges, higher tariffs, elevated freight costs, and potential customer traffic slowdowns could pressure Burlington's margins.

Meanwhile, Burlington's transition toward smaller 25,000-27,000-square-foot stores is intended to improve sales productivity, but execution risks and rising costs remain potential headwinds, especially after the company has missed revenue expectations in two of its last four quarterly reports.

BURL Forms a Death Cross

Adding to its bearish outlook, Burlington's technical chart indicates mounting selling pressure, with BURL trading well below its 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages of approximately $262 and $306 a share, respectively.

More concerning, the 50-day SMA (green line below) has fallen below the 200-day SMA (red line), forming a bearish death cross pattern that suggests weakening momentum and the potential for further downside.

With BURL approaching its recent 52-week lows near $226, the stock could remain under pressure until buying interest returns and its technical trend improves.

Burlington's Mediocre Valuation

Even after falling nearly 20% year-to-date, Burlington shares still command a forward P/E multiple near 20X. This is roughly on par with, but not a discount to its Zacks Retail-Discount Stores industry average, which includes noteworthy peers such as Ross Stores () and The TJX Companies ().  

While Burlington has opportunities to expand its store footprint and capture market share in the off-price retail segment, the trend of declining EPS revisions is taking away from its modest valuation and leaves shares vulnerable to further selling pressure if earnings expectations continue to decline.

Bottom Line

Burlington Stores stock currently lands a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), reflecting the unfavorable trend in earnings estimate revisions.

With profitability expectations weakening and shares offering little valuation discount to industry peers, BURL may be a stock investors want to avoid for now, particularly until earnings revisions stabilize.

Additional content:
Spotify Stock Rises +6% Despite Reporting Q3 Earnings Miss

Spotify Technology S.A. reported mixed third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted earnings missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate while revenues beat expectations.

Despite the earnings miss, the stock has gained 5.7% since the earnings release on Oct. 22.

Adjusted earnings of $2.85 per share missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.10 by 8.1%. Higher marketing, cloud infrastructure and artificial intelligence spending weighed on profitability.

Revenues rose 16% year over year in euros and 14% at constant currency to $5.72 billion. The figure surpassed the consensus estimate of $5.70 billion by 0.35%. Premium subscribers reached 306 million, exceeding management's guidance by 1 million, while advertising growth accelerated.

SPOT's User Growth Remains Strong

Monthly active users, or MAUs, increased 11% year over year and 1% sequentially to 788 million. Spotify added 11 million MAUs during the quarter, matching management's guidance. Growth was recorded across all regions, led by sequential gains in Rest of World, Latin America, Europe and North America.

Premium subscribers rose 9% year over year and 2% sequentially. Net additions totaled 6 million, supported by global promotional campaigns and partnerships. Ad-supported MAUs increased 12% year over year to 499 million, reflecting continued audience expansion.

Spotify's Premium Revenues Gain Momentum

Premium revenues increased 17% year over year to €4.49 billion, or 15% at constant currency. Growth was supported by subscriber additions and higher average revenue per user, or ARPU, reflecting benefits from pricing actions.

Premium ARPU increased 9.3% year over year to €4.95, or 7.5% excluding currency movements. Price increases supported monetization, although product and geographic mix partially offset the benefits. Premium gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 34.5%, aided by revenue growth outpacing content costs.

SPOT's Margins Expand Despite Higher Costs

Gross profit increased 21% year over year to €1.64 billion. The gross margin expanded 136 basis points to 33%, exceeding management's guidance of 32.9%. Improvements across Premium and Ad-Supported operations supported the expansion.

Operating expenses increased 26% year over year to €967 million. Excluding currency movements and social charges, expenses rose 19%, primarily reflecting elevated marketing, cloud and AI investments. Operating income increased 15% to €672 million, while the operating margin declined to 13.5% from 13.6%.

Social charges totaled €22 million, exceeding management's forecast by €13 million due to share-price movements. Lower-than-expected marketing and personnel costs, alongside gross margin outperformance, partially offset the impact.

Spotify's Advertising Business Shows Recovery

Ad-supported revenues increased 10% year over year to €482 million, representing 9% growth at constant currency. This marked an improvement from the 3% constant-currency growth recorded in each of the first two quarters of 2026.

Music advertising benefited from higher impressions sold, partially offset by softer pricing. Podcast advertising gained from stronger sponsorship activity across Spotify's owned and licensed content portfolio. Automated sales channels remained the largest contributors to advertising growth.

Management highlighted continued progress in rebuilding its advertising infrastructure. Biddable channels accounted for approximately 40% of advertising revenues, supporting the company's efforts to improve monetization and advertising efficiency.

SPOT's Cash Flow Supports Share Repurchases

The free cash flow declined 9% year over year to €735 million, reflecting unfavorable working-capital movements and cash-tax timing. Trailing 12-month free cash flow totaled €3.2 billion, demonstrating the company's sustained cash-generation capacity.

Spotify ended the quarter with €9.9 billion in cash, restricted cash and short-term investments. From the start of 2026 through Oct. 21, the company repurchased 2.2 million shares for $1.1 billion, fully offsetting dilution from employee equity programs and returning additional excess cash to shareholders.

Spotify Guides for Continued Q4 Growth

For fourth-quarter 2026, Spotify expects 818 million MAUs, implying 30 million sequential additions. Premium subscribers are projected to reach 316 million, representing 10 million net additions.

Revenues are forecast at €5.2 billion, supported by pricing actions and audiobook add-on monetization. Management expects advertising growth to continue progressing toward double-digit levels, while operating expense growth moderates.

Spotify anticipates a gross margin of 33.8% and operating income of €820 million. Management expects continued benefits from AI-driven personalization, audiobook expansion to more than 180 markets and broader podcast monetization initiatives, while maintaining expense discipline into 2027.

SPOT currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Earnings Snapshot

Equifax's third-quarter 2026 earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate, while revenues met the same.

EFX's adjusted earnings were $2.26 per share, up 10.8% year over year. The figure topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.19 by 3.2%. Revenues increased 9.6% year over year to $1.69 billion, in line with the consensus estimate.

ManpowerGroup reported mixed third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted earnings meeting the Zacks Consensus Estimate and revenues missing expectations.

MAN's adjusted earnings of $1.01 per share were in line with the consensus estimate and increased 22% year over year. Revenues of $4.84 billion lagged the consensus estimate of $4.91 billion by 1.4% but increased 4% year over year (5% in constant currency).

title: Is Trending Stock Spotify Technology (SPOT) a Buy Now?
detail:
Is Trending Stock Spotify Technology (SPOT) a Buy Now?
Zacks Equity Research
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 7:00 AM CDT 5 min read
SPOT
^GSPC
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Spotify (SPOT) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Shares of this music-streaming service operator have returned +12.5% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -0.2% change. The Zacks Internet - Software industry, to which Spotify belongs, has lost 7.1% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Spotify is expected to post earnings of $3.78 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of -26.7%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +2.4%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $13.74 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +15.6%. This estimate has changed -0.7% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $16.13 indicates a change of +17.4% from what Spotify is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -7.7%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) for Spotify.

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS
12-month consensus EPS estimate for SPOT
Projected Revenue Growth

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.

In the case of Spotify, the consensus sales estimate of $5.85 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +11%. The $22.05 billion and $25.16 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +13.5% and +14.1%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Spotify reported revenues of $5.72 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +14.5%. EPS of $2.85 for the same period compares with $3.83 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.7 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +0.31%. The EPS surprise was -8.06%.

Over the last four quarters, Spotify surpassed consensus EPS estimates two times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates two times over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

Comparing the current value of a company's valuation multiples, such as its price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), to its own historical values helps ascertain whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, whereas comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of how reasonable its stock price is.

As part of the Zacks Style Scores system, the Zacks Value Style Score (which evaluates both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics) organizes stocks into five groups ranging from A to F (A is better than B; B is better than C; and so on), making it helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Spotify is graded D on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Conclusion

Key Takeaways

Jefferies raised its Spotify price target to $620 from $600 and called the platform highly defensible against AI, while the stock is down 8.5% in 2026.

Margins are the best test of that call, because a business losing ground to AI shouldn't be able to keep raising prices and keep more of every euro.

Spotify guided to a 32.9% gross margin and €670 million of operating income for the third quarter, after 33.4% and €655 million in the second.

At about 35x forward earnings, the stock gets cheaper quickly if margins keep climbing, though a soft subscriber count or Q4 outlook could still overshadow a strong margin print.

Spotify (SPOT:NYSE) stock is down 8.5% in 2026 (through Tuesday's close), as investors worry about what AI could do to a subscription music business.

Jefferies thinks the market has it wrong, and Spotify gets its chance to show which side is right when it reports third-quarter results before the open on Thursday, Oct. 22.

What Jefferies is betting on

On Tuesday, Jefferies kept its Buy rating and raised its price target to $620 from $600, about 18% above Tuesday's close. Analyst James Heaney called Spotify's platform "highly defensible against AI disintermediation fears."

His reasons: expectations are muted, he expects operating expense growth to peak this quarter, and he sees advertising improving as programmatic sales become a bigger part of the business. (Ads could use the help: ad-supported revenue grew just 1% in the second quarter.) He also expects price increases in the US and UK within the next six to 12 months.

Then there's the AI angle. Jefferies sees a possible launch announcement later this year for an AI-powered remixing product tied to Spotify's partnership with Warner Music Group. But its base case includes no AI revenue at all, so none of that $620 depends on AI paying off.

If AI were really pulling listeners away from Spotify, pricing is where you'd see it first. People who have somewhere better to go don't keep paying more.

Spotify's subscribers keep paying more. In the second quarter, Premium revenue grew 15% to €4.33 billion, from 9% more subscribers and 7% higher revenue per user.

Those price increases have widened the gross margin, from 25.0% in 2022 to 32.0% in 2025…

title: Is Spotify Technology SA a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report?

Is Spotify Technology SA a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report?
Eric Volkman, The Motley Fool

Spotify Technology (NYSE:SPOT) not only saw its third-quarter headline net income fall, but it also whiffed on the consensus analyst estimate. Given that, you'd imagine that investors would have reacted by aggressively selling the music streamer's stock. Well, you'd be very wrong.

The opposite occurred on Thursday after the company published its earnings release -- market players couldn't wait to buy its stock, and it handily beat the S&P 500 index, rising nearly 4%. On Friday, it ticked higher. Let's look at the company's numbers and tease out why it scored such a big win from an ostensibly losing quarter.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Music to their ears

Spotify's quarter was headed by a revenue line that hit almost 5 billion euros ($5.6 billion), for robust year-over-year growth of 16%. By far the bulk of the company's top line comes from its premium services; the take from these rose by 17% to nearly 4.5 billion euros ($5 billion). The remainder came from ad-supported offerings, which collectively rose 10% to 482 million euros ($540 million).

Spotify also managed to grow both its total user base and the crucial segment of that population, premium-service subscribers. The company's total monthly active user (MAU) count rose 11% to 788 million, while the premium subscriber tally increased 9% to 306 million.

Attributable net income, however, went in the opposite direction. It fell to 518 million euros ($580 million) from the year-ago profit of 899 million euros ($1 billion). On a per-share basis, the former result was 2.48 euros ($2.78).

While that revenue number was essentially in line with the consensus analyst estimate, Spotify fell short on profitability. Analysts tracking the stock were modeling net income of 2.84 euros ($3.18) for the quarter.

That bottom-line swoon looked ugly on paper, but it wasn't as grim as it appeared. In the third quarter of 2025, the company benefited enormously from significant finance income derived from share, bond, and warrant valuations, which affected the accounting. It also recorded a 72 million euro ($81 million) tax benefit during that period.

Spotify watchers are aware that these items distorted the 2025 frame's profitability, so the year-over-year drop wasn't particularly concerning to them. They were also impressed that the company topped its guidance for operating income, which came in at 672 million euros ($753 million), and notched a new record for gross margin at 33%. And for a stock increasingly evaluated on free cash flow (FCF), the 735 million euros ($823 million) in FCF it generated during the quarter was heartening.

Streaming forward

Spotify has an enviably high number of growth opportunities. Management ticked off several major ones, including a major expansion of its relatively recent audiobook business, from the current 22 countries to over 180. Meanwhile, artificial intelligence (AI) is at a relatively early stage of deployment for the company; it plans to harness it to offer subscribers more and increasingly varied custom services -- AI playlists, anyone? -- to enhance the listening and music-curating experiences.

It's confident that this will keep those subscriber and fundamental numbers rising. It proffered guidance for its current (fourth) quarter of 818 million MAUs, which, if achieved, would be nearly 9% higher than in the same period of 2025. It's also counting on a sub-9% increase in premium subscribers (to 316 million). As for key financials, management is expecting another pop in revenue, by almost 15% to 5.2 billion euros ($5.8 billion). Operating income is projected to surge 17% to 820 million euros ($919 million). It did not provide a net income forecast.

I feel that, if anything, Mr. Market's reaction to Spotify's third quarter was muted and conservative. The company has established itself as the clear king of streaming music and, increasingly, other aural entertainment options like audiobooks. I feel it's building quite the imposing moat, which more than justifies the valuations that likely moderated investors' reaction to the earnings release (its forward P/E is approaching 52). Yet this company is becoming ever more powerful, and it clearly aims to tap into the numerous, high-potential growth opportunities before it. I'd be a buyer of this stock, even at its seemingly lofty level.

What Happened?

Analysts raised their Spotify Technology (SPOT:NYSE) price targets on October 22 and 23, yet three of the new targets still sit below the stock's closing price. Shares jumped 11.10% to $583.66 on October 22 after a third-quarter report that beat subscriber guidance and forecast fourth-quarter profit above estimates, on a day the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6%. The move took the stock from about 9.5% below its 2025 year-end close of $580.71 to about 0.5% above it.

Three New Targets Already Trail the Stock

Benzinga's October 23 roundup lists three changes: Cantor Fitzgerald to $550 from $490 and Rosenblatt to $576 from $527, both Neutral, and Guggenheim to $650 from $575 with a Buy. Cantor had cut its target to $490 from $530 on October 12, per TipRanks. Pivotal Research moved to $460 from $420 with a Hold, about 21% below the close, per TipRanks, which also reported Barclays at $650 and Wells Fargo at $660. Raymond James went to $625, per StreetInsider.

Whatever moved those targets, it was not a bigger revenue forecast. TIKR's consensus for fiscal 2027 revenue rose only 0.31% between September 30 and October 23, to about €22.4 billion, while fiscal 2026 slipped 0.13%.

Spotify Analyst Estimates Trend – Revenue (TIKR)

TIKR's Street mean stood at $611.77 on October 22, about $28 above the close, within a range of $459.79 to $720.89. The rating mix shifted between September 30 and October 22, from 24 Buys, 8 Outperforms and 7 Holds to 22 Buys, 9 Outperforms and 9 Holds. The quarter itself missed on two lines: revenue by 0.2%, and GAAP earnings per share of €2.48 against €2.81, a gap TIKR's earnings-day coverage traced to items below operating income.

Spotify Street Targets (TIKR)
Spotify's Co-CEO Bets It Will Be the Last Subscription Users Cancel

Analyst Rich Greenfield asked on the call whether AI agents that compare prices and cancel unused subscriptions could turn Spotify into an interchangeable back-end pipe. Co-CEO Gustav Söderström answered that Spotify has run in the background of Google Maps and Waze for years and grew through it, because the business earns money even when its app is not on screen.

He said more than 100 million users use Spotify roughly 28 days a month, then added: "It's a bold bet but I think on that list of things that you unsubscribe from, Spotify is going to be the last thing that you unsubscribe from." That is a management prediction, not churn data, but heavy daily use is what an agent hunting for forgotten subscriptions would spare.
